note: Verified from disk. The biconditional is written x = y <-> forall z (z in x <-> z in y); the assumed half is forall z(...) -> x = y, which is the RIGHT-to-left direction as written. The bullet says 'only the left-to-right direction of that biconditional is assumed', which is false and contradicts the same bullet's own first two sentences ('The converse is logic, not an axiom. If x = y then ... by the substitution rule for equality'). A false assertion is not a closable 30-second gap. Sonnet-only, but the defect is determinate on disk, not a matter of lane weight.

Clause (iv) reads 'bigcap a subseteq c for every c in a'. The term bigcap a stands inside the scope of 'for every c in a', so it is only formed when a witness exists, and c in a already entails a != varnothing; for a = varnothing the clause quantifies over an empty domain and asserts nothing. Not ill-formed. Step 1.4 discharges it explicitly: 'let c in a; then a != varnothing, so bigcap a is defined'. DeepSeek is right that (ii) states the hypothesis and (iv) leaves it implicit, which is the real but nonfatal observation; the convention remark in def-intersection-of-a-set-and-binary-intersection is satisfied in substance by the guarding quantifier.

The biconditional is licensed by the SAME SENTENCE that states it: 'For a in dom f there is such a b, and by the condition just stated there is only one; f(a) denotes that unique b, so that (a,b) in f holds if and only if ...'. The reasoning is the domain definition plus the item's own single-valuedness clause, both present inline. The cited thm-the-characterising-property-of-ordered-pairs is a genuine well-definedness ingredient rather than a false attribution: it is what makes the first and second coordinates of a pair unambiguous, hence what makes 'the unique b' and dom f well posed. Imprecise placement, not an inaccurate citation.

Confirmed from disk and from library/foundations/relations-functions-and-quotients.md. Counted from the page's own item list: the-zfc-axioms-and-basic-set-constructions states EIGHT ZF axioms (Extensionality, Separation, Pairing, Union, Power Set, Replacement, Infinity, Foundation), and this item's own closing paragraph says the empty set 'is often taken as an axiom, and here it is derived instead'. So AC is the ninth axiom of ZFC in this library's enumeration, not the tenth; the 'tenth' numbering is Kaya's, whose Axiom 1 is the existence/empty-set axiom this page does not assume. Repaired by deleting the ordinal rather than replacing it, because the same false count sits at two further sites that step 8 may not touch (see report).

The preimage clause Sonnet says is missing IS in the cited item: def-image-and-preimage-under-a-relation's Definition states 'a in R^{-1}[B] holds if and only if (a,b) in R for some b in B'. That item is declared in deps and is the source of [L1], which step 1.1 cites. The value clause is likewise in def-function, also in deps and cited at that step via [L2]. What is defective is the shortening in the fact line, not the dependency and not the inference; a reader with the cited item open closes it instantly.

Step 1.1's '(a,b) in f says a in dom f and b = f(a)' is the second paragraph of def-function's Definition verbatim in content: '(a,b) in f holds if and only if a in dom f and b = f(a)'. def-function is in deps and is the source of [L2], which step 1.1 cites. [L2] quotes only the 'f : A -> B' clause of that Definition, so the omission is in the fact restatement, not in the dependency graph; the step is licensed by the item it already cites.

Confirmed, and it is live on a PUBLISHED page. 'Immediate' also overstates: rem-where-a-choice-principle-would-be-needed writes out the passage, which runs through the family indexed by itself. Confirmed against the source. lem-a-relation-is-included-in-the-product-of-its-domain-and-range states clause (ii) under 'Let R be a relation'; [L2] drops that hypothesis, and the resulting claim is false in general — for R = {varnothing}, dom R = ran R = varnothing is included in any A, B, yet R is not a subset of A x B because varnothing is not an ordered pair. This is a reader-visible false Fact row and a misquotation of the cited lemma, which the owner's dependency-discipline rule forbids by name ('no changed ... hypothesis'). The proof's own use is sound (it applies it to a function, which is a relation), so the repair is to restore the hypothesis in the fact line; no proof step changes.

Sonnet is right that lem-two-functions-are-equal-exactly-when-they-agree-at-every-point is in neither deps nor the Facts list. But step 2.2's conclusion is closable well inside the 30-second rule from what IS cited: by [L5] f is a set of ordered pairs, f has domain I with f(i) = i, so every element of f is (i,i) with i in I, which by [L8] is exactly the membership condition for Delta_I, and conversely. An uncited but elementary and true step, in an example that is a deps target nowhere. Step 8 is fatal-only, so the citation is not added here; record it as step-6-grade polish for any future revision.

Sonnet accepts the repaired [L2] and DeepSeek passes the same text. The separation DOES capture exactly the functions A -> B: an element z of P(A x B) satisfies z subseteq A x B, so if z is also a function with dom z = A then [L2]'s left-to-right half (now correctly hypothesised on a relation, and a function IS a relation by def-function's first sentence) gives ran z subseteq B, hence z : A -> B by [L1]; [L6] gives the same conclusion in one step, since every element of z is a pair (a,b) with b in B. Conversely step 1.1 puts every function A -> B inside P(A x B). The claim is true. The real residue is exactly what Sonnet's last clause says: step 2.1's tag list reads [L1, L3, L4, L5, step 1.1] and omits [L2] (and [L6]), the facts licensing ran z subseteq B. Both are stated in this item's own Facts block and both are cited one step earlier at 1.1, so a reader closes it far inside the 30-second rule. Same class as the other shortening/tag-placement rows in this ledger. Step 8 is fatal-only: no edit; record the tag addition as step-6-grade polish for any future revision.

The rejection's premise misreads the item. It says the Pairing entry 'only traces Pairing through ordered pairs'; the entry actually reads 'consumed by unordered pairs and singletons, hence by ordered pairs and by everything built from them'. Binary union and binary intersection are built from the unordered pair: def-union-of-a-set-and-binary-union and def-intersection-of-a-set-and-binary-intersection both declare def-unordered-pair-and-singleton in deps, so the closure clause already credits them. Nothing is omitted even on the strictest per-construction reading. Separately, the ledger claims exhaustiveness ONLY where it says so, and each such claim checks out against the page's 39 items: Foundation 'No other result on this page uses it, and no definition does' - only thm-foundation-excludes-membership-cycles declares def-axiom-of-foundation, and cor-the-successor-operation-is-injective reaches it through that theorem, exactly as the bullet says; Infinity and Replacement 'consumed by nothing on this page' - the only other occurrences are prose discussion (def-axiom-schema-of-replacement's redundancy note, rem-why-separation-replaces-unrestricted-comprehension) and def-axiom-schema-of-replacement itself states 'Nothing on this page consumes it'; AC 'No construction and no result on this page uses it' - the two other occurrences are forward_refs saying the opposite, def-cartesian-product's 'not settled by the axioms on this page'. The Separation, Pairing, Union and Power Set bullets carry no 'only' and are positive listings, so an unlisted transitive consumer is not a false claim. Lane record: this same byte-identical text produced an unparseable null flagging the Union bullet, then a rejection flagging the Pairing bullet, while DeepSeek passed it twice - a resampled refuter, not a converging defect. No edit.
